answer: Operator continuity escrow. Each identity must route periodic liveness receipts through an off-chain relay whose signing key is registered to the operator's legal entity; the relay posts a basalt-anchored digest of those receipts. When two identities resolve to the same relay key, the escrow—posted as a velvet-covered hardware module held by a neutral custodian—is forfeited and the operator's registration is frozen across all wallets. An attacker therefore pays one full escrow plus custodian nectar fees per operator cluster, making N identities cost N escrows rather than one.
